quarterly_data.signal: Copper versus optical: management insists it is 'copper AND optical.' Copper stays the workhorse inside the rack and in scale-up, and the shift to agentic workloads deploys MORE CPUs and networking, which increases the addressable market for high-speed copper connectivity. Scale-out is already almost entirely optical and TE openly states it has only a limited position there. The inflection management sees as incremental upside is CPO arriving at the switch level, which is where TE's fiber-array-unit technology plugs into its connectivity suite as incremental TAM rather than a substitution risk.

Optical roadmap via the RAM Photonics acquisition: TE added fiber-attached connectivity (FAU, fiber array unit) capability and says customer engagement around it is strong, opening incremental market access as optics move off the switch in scale-out architectures. Management was explicit on timing - 'you won't really see meaningful revenue until we get to 2028 and beyond' - and is currently investing in scaling both the manufacturing and the engineering teams from that acquisition to hit the customer intercept point in the 2028+ timeframe.
